text:
alex: Heads-up — I reproduced the weird H2D/D2H jitter on small-batch (B=1) runs. It correlates with KV cache eviction bursts and our new kernel selection heuristic. Timeline attached from nsys.
riley: repro steps? config? which model + quantization?

alex: repro steps below:
```bash
# env
BATCH_SIZE=1 PYTORCH_JIT=0 \
  REDWOOD_KVCACHE=local REDWOOD_ALLOC_PINNED=0 \
  python run_inference.py --model rwd-ggml-q4_0 --sequence 1024 --warmup 10 --iter 200

# profiling
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=tmp/kv-evict-b1 -- python run_inference.py ...
```
Small/fast requests + frequent cache evictions. Observed lots of small cudaMemcpy Async calls interleaved with page_fault events.

sam: this smells like the kernel selector change (PR #432) that prefers the single-stream low-latency kernel for short seqs. That kernel issues more small H2D bursts instead of coalesced batches.

jordan: nsys summary (trimmed):
```
Total GPU kernels: 3300
H2D transfers: 1.18 GB (many small chunks, 4-64 KB)
D2H transfers: 620 MB
cudaMemcpyAsync avg latency: 120us (tail 800us)
Host page_fault events: 430 spikes correlated with H2D calls
CPU wait on ioctl/pci_dma: visible in timeline
```
Timeline shows alternating tiny H2D submits that keep the PCIe engine busy and prevent bulk DMA coalescing. Also see repeated page faults when pageable buffers are pinned on-demand.

perf-ci-bot: perf-alert: regression detected on branch "kernel-selector-v2" — p99 latency +12% on kv-evict workload. See: https://ci.internal/reports/1809

riley: quick experiments to try: toggle REDWOOD_ALLOC_PINNED=1 (force pinned allocations), and increase batching window to 8ms to let the runtime coalesce transfers. Also try forcing the older batched kernel.

sam: agree. If pinned reduces page_faults we avoid the on-demand pinning penalty — but pinned memory increases host-side copy cost and fragmentation. We should measure both tail and throughput.

alex: I ran an A/B this morning. Results (single-node, same load):
```
A: pageable (default)  p99=220ms  mean=85ms  H2D bursts=~3300
B: pinned allocator     p99=160ms  mean=92ms  H2D bursts reduced by ~70%
Notes: pinned increased host memcpy CPU time by ~30% but removed page_fault spikes and reduced small DMA submits.
```

jordan: attached short perfetto slice: pinned trace shows larger, fewer DMA ops. Pageable trace shows many small DMA ops with gaps where the CPU waits for pin + ioctl.

alex: actionable items: 1) add kv-eviction perf harness (B=1, hot cache churn) in perf repo; 2) add heuristic: if eviction_rate > 5% then prefer pinned allocator + batched kernel; 3) revert the kernel-selector fallback until we validate on this workload.

riley: +1 on the harness. I'll file the config change as a feature flag so we can toggle at runtime.

sam: I'll sketch the heuristic and bench matrix (pinned vs pageable, batching windows 1/4/8/16ms, kernel A vs B) and post results by EOD.

jordan: volunteered to run a larger scale A/B in staging, I'll attach nsys timelines and perfstats.

alex: thanks — let's not auto-apply pinned by default, but enable it as a routing option for eviction-heavy requests. After we have perf harness and regression tests we can decide on default. :thumbsup:

perf-ci-bot: noted. created issue PERF-1187 and CI job perf/kv-evict (scheduled).

alex: one more note — consider adding a tiny transfer coalescer in the runtime: collect short-lived H2D submissions for up to X us and flush as one DMA if latency budget allows. Might be lower-risk than pinned by default.

riley: good call. I'll prototype a 32-128us coalescing window and test.
